title: 22. Public Sector Enterprises & Disinvestment Architecture
summary: Public Sector Enterprises are classified under financial autonomy tiers, while state disinvestment policies manage privatization and strategic asset sales via DIPAM.

blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: Public Sector Enterprises are classified under financial autonomy tiers, while state disinvestment policies manage privatization and strategic asset sales via DIPAM.

blocks.content: 1. Financial Autonomy Tiers: Maharatna (Investment delegation up to ₹5,000 Cr) | Navratna (up to ₹1,000 Cr) | Miniratna Category I & II.
2. Types of Disinvestment: Minority Disinvestment (Govt retains $>51%$ stake & management control) vs Strategic Disinvestment (Govt sells $>50%$ stake AND transfers management control).
3. Institutional Nodal Body: **DIPAM** (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management) under Ministry of Finance.
4. New PSE Policy (2021): Classifies sectors into **Strategic** (Bare minimum 1 CPSE retained) and **Non-Strategic** (All CPSEs to be privatized or closed).

blocks.text:
⚡ 1. Criteria for Maharatna Status Eligibility
To qualify for **Maharatna** status, a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) MUST fulfill:
1. Hold **Navratna** status.
2. Listed on Indian stock exchange under SEBI regulations.
3. Average annual net profit $> mathbf{	ext{₹}2,500	ext{ Crore}}$ during last 3 years.
4. Average annual Net Worth $> mathbf{	ext{₹}15,000	ext{ Crore}}$ during last 3 years.
5. Average annual Turnover $> mathbf{	ext{₹}25,000	ext{ Crore}}$ during last 3 years.
6. Significant global footprint/international operations.

📖 2. Types of Disinvestment & NITI Aayog Role
- **Minority Disinvestment:** Selling minority equity (e.g. IPO / OFS) while retaining $ge 51%$ shareholding and executive management control.
- **Strategic Disinvestment:** Sale of 50% or more of government equity in a CPSE along with **transfer of management control** to a private strategic partner (e.g., Air India sale to Tata Group in 2022).
- **NITI Aayog Role:** Recommends CPSEs for strategic disinvestment to the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA).

🏛️ 3. New Public Sector Enterprise Policy (Budget 2021-22)
Classifies CPSEs into two broad categories:
1. **Strategic Sectors (4 Groups):** Atomic Energy/Space/Defense; Transport/Telecom; Power/Petroleum/Coal/Minerals; Banking/Insurance/Financial Services. *Bare minimum 1 CPSE will be retained; others merged or privatized.*
2. **Non-Strategic Sectors:** CPSEs in all other sectors will be privatized or closed down.

⚖️ 4. Common Prelims & Mains Traps
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** In Strategic Disinvestment, management control MUST be transferred to the private buyer along with equity sale. Selling 10% equity without transferring management is minority disinvestment!
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** DIPAM is a department under the **Ministry of Finance** (formerly Department of Disinvestment; renamed DIPAM in 2016).

blocks.content:
#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Which nodal department under the Ministry of Finance manages government equity investments, disinvestments, and asset monetization in CPSEs?  
(A) Department of Economic Affairs (DEA)  
(B) Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)  
(C) Department of Financial Services (DFS)  
(D) NITI Aayog  
**Answer:** **(B)** — DIPAM manages disinvestment and public asset monetization.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** Government sells 53.29% stake in BPCL to a private entity along with transfer of management control. Identify the exact category of disinvestment.  
**Resolution:** This is **Strategic Disinvestment**, because over 50% equity is transferred AND management control is handed over to the private purchaser.

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Evaluate the New Public Sector Enterprise Policy 2021. Differentiate between Minority Disinvestment and Strategic Disinvestment with recent Indian case studies.'*
